user_requirement: Never dip below 60 FPS; no average/percentile-only pass while individual measured frames exceed 1000/60 ms.

active_policy.overrides: Launcher arguments above this ceiling are rejected. Direct probe/menu settings are capped; zero/nonfinite values cannot disable the gate.
active_policy.warmup: Frame/action limits include running warmup observations; no warmup exemption.

decision.problem: The former 100 ms alarm allowed severe visible stutters; historical passes did not establish smooth 60 FPS. A 60 FPS test cap includes deliberate waiting in wall-frame samples.
principles: Tail/worst-frame latency instead of average-only throughput
Separate capacity measurement from deliberate pacing
Preserve failures and stop interrupted test sequences
decision.choice: Enforce 1000/60 ms for measured frames and synchronous actions. Request uncapped, VSync-disabled performance runs, retain raw intervals and stop/log the first issue. Stop sending pointer input or checking final poses once a performance failure has paused that sequence.
decision.owner: Shared Budget constants/helper, validated launcher arguments, existing scene-owned probes/menu suite.

alternatives.assessment: Rejected: contradicts the user requirement and hides isolated spikes.

alternatives.option: Subtract a guessed pacing allowance from capped frames
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: can hide actual work. Uncap measurement and preserve raw wall intervals.

alternatives.option: Loosen limits, drop elapsed work or change gameplay cadence
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: preserve correctness, progress and workloads.

evidence: Existing E15 captures include 62.347 ms live ticks and 51.959 ms settlement.
Service-level capture below observes opening-policy and planning/admission spikes.
Three real rejection/pause/log contracts pass, including attempted 100 ms environment overrides.
Actual uncapped 1x tests fail at 25.236 ms with profiling and 22.572 ms without it.
tradeoffs: Uncapped input stress generates more events than a capped run; it is a new baseline, not an optimization comparison.
VSync disabling is requested; driver enforcement can override it. Engine cap and flags are recorded.
Wall intervals include scheduling/rendering. Preserve over-budget observations; no outlier allowance is used to pass.
Profiler costs and nested inclusive scopes require separate attribution/acceptance modes.
No gameplay scheduler/strategy optimization is claimed in this policy change. The application still fails.
decision.acceptance: Enforcement guards pass; game compliance is false. Every measured frame/action must satisfy the ceiling in declared native scenarios with correctness/progress gates before claiming compliance.
decision.rollback: Retain the user 60 FPS requirement and all raw evidence. Measurement/configuration changes are independently reversible; do not restore 100 ms to obtain passes.

service_attribution.settings: Captured before defaults changed: old 100 ms alarm, 60 FPS cap, counters on, stacks off, stage timings on. Its legacy PASS is not a 60 FPS pass.
service_attribution.interpretation: Opening policy max 46.726 ms; battlefield settlement 49.354 ms; planning/admission-labelled pure_work 21.255 ms; live tick 63.342 ms. These nested inclusive wall scopes must not be summed or labelled self CPU time. pure_work may include admission; source review is required before changing it.
